decisions.statement: A route here answers a signed-in reader alone.
How many pages a page type has is the count the pages answer with rather than the rows carried.
A listing has five thousand rows at the most.
That ceiling is stated in the question rather than trimmed off the answer.
A listing carries a page's own values and not the rows filed beside that page.
The keys a listing asks for are named in the question rather than trimmed after.
The page type is read before the pages are asked, so the question can name keys.
An answer says how many pages were counted and whether the listing reached those pages.
A question the pages refuse is answered 503 with the refusal's own words.
A listing whose roster will not read is answered 501 with the reason that roster went unread.
The roster names every page type `@akasha/page-service` has pages for.
A roster entry has that page type's slug alone.
A page type's row has the property definitions that page type declares.
A row of any other page type has no property definition.
A page type whose properties went unread carries no definition rather than refusing the listing.
A page type with no definition is told apart from a page type with an empty list.
A roster that will not read is answered 503 with the reason that roster went unread.
A raise that is not the roster's is left to raise.
An unanswered question is never reported as a page type holding nothing.
A roster entry names no repository and no glob.

definition: what a page or page-type query is answered with
